selectedReplayRule: Current required authorization precedes replay; exact authorized retries resolve the original accepted result using the selected logical identity and immutable actor/intent/source binding. Fresh mutable feasibility, clock selection and body preparation cannot replace that original result. Expected revision is concurrency precondition, not a new identity.

productRules.rule: An external consultant hired directly by a client gets a guest membership limited to programs the Org Admin grants, with no approval rights and a required end date.
The guest end date is persisted on the guest Member registration, access stops at the end of that UTC date, and later grant proposals cannot extend beyond it.
Each Membership records exactly one affiliation: client_personnel, firm_staff, or guest.
Deprovisioning permanently terminates one membership episode in one tenant; it is terminal and distinct from reversible suspension, and a deprovisioned person cannot be reinstated.
A fresh invitation after deprovisioning creates a new membership episode, and only after the prior episode's tenant authority cleanup completes.
The deprovision command records actor, timestamp, and reason.

A new invitation never restores old team assignments or member-scoped grants; each direct member grant is bound to the membership episode active when issued, so retained or delayed grant history from a prior episode cannot become effective after rejoining.

decides: Affiliation is exactly one of client_personnel, firm_staff, or guest; a guest requires a finite end date, persisted on the registration, access stops at the end of that UTC date, and grants cannot extend beyond it (guests are limited to Org Admin-granted programs and hold no approval rights). Deprovision records actor, timestamp, and reason, refuses self-deprovisioning, and removes team assignments and member-scoped grants prospectively while retaining platform identity, Person, history, business records, and unfinished work. A new invitation never restores old assignments or grants; each direct grant is bound to the episode active when issued, so prior-episode grants cannot become effective after rejoining.
